Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 42, verses 10–12:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment is with Allah﴾: that is, of matters of religion and of worldly affairs, whether with the disbelievers or with the believers.

﴿Its judgment is with Allah﴾: He is the One who decides it in this world by what is revealed as wahy (revelation) to His Messenger, and in the Hereafter, since judgment belongs to Him alone and to no other.

﴿That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn in repentance﴾: that is, say to them, O Our Messenger: That is the Judge, the Just and Mighty, Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, meaning I have entrusted my affairs to Him, and to Him alone, not to anyone else, do I return in all my affairs.

﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, their Originator and Innovator, without any prior pattern.

﴿He has made for you from yourselves mates, and among the livestock, mates﴾: that is, by making you male and female, and likewise [He made] for the livestock.

﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾: that is, He creates you through this arrangement, which consists of male and female, He brings you forth.

﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾: that is, nothing is like Allah, for He is the Creator of everything, so no created thing can ever be like Him in any state whatsoever.

﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾: that is, He hears the words of His servants and knows their deeds and conditions.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, says: Whatever you differ about, O people, of matters of religion and worldly affairs, its judgment is with Allah, the Exalted. He is the One who judges it with justice, so refer it back to Him, glorified and exalted, for He judges between you with truth. Here He commands His Messenger to say to the polytheists: That, described by the attributes of majesty and perfection, is the Just Judge who decides and is not decided against: Allah, my Lord, the One who has no lord besides Him. Upon Him I have relied, having entrusted my affairs to Him, confident in His sufficiency, and to Him alone I turn in repentance, meaning I return to Him in all my affairs. Then He continued to mention His attributes of action, saying: Creator of the heavens and the earth, that is, the Creator of the seven heavens and the earth and their Originator without any prior pattern. ﴿He has made for you from yourselves mates﴾, for He created Eve from the rib of Adam, then made you reproduce from male and female. And among the livestock, mates as well, namely the male and the female. His saying ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ means He creates you within it, that is, within this system of male and female, as if maleness and femaleness were a factory in which the creation of humans and animals is completed. Glory be to the Creator, the All-Knowing.

His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾: this is a description by which Exalted Allah made Himself known so that He would be recognized among His servants, namely that He, Mighty and Majestic, has nothing like Him, that is, nothing is like Him. Thus He was described by singularity of oneness. The One who has no equal and to whom nothing is similar is Allah, Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names and the Highest Attributes, and He is the All-Hearing of all voices, the All-Knowing of all beings.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, to Him belong the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and the locks of them. He expands provision for whomever He wills as a trial, and restricts it as a test, for He is All-Knowing of everything, so one should seek provision from Him alone and turn to none but Him for it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to refer what is disputed to Allah, the Exalted, that He may judge it, which is the referral to the Book and the Sunnah.

2- The obligation to rely upon Him and turn to Him in repentance in all matters.

3- Exalting Allah above resembling His creation, together with the obligation to believe in His Most Beautiful Names and Highest Attributes.

4- The obligation to believe that Allah is the Provider, in whose hand are the keys to the treasuries of provision: whoever He wills, He widens provision for, and whoever He wills, He restricts it for, and that He widens for one wisdom and restricts for another.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 42, verses 15–16**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"So for that, invite"* (﴿فَلِذَلِكَ فَٱدْعُ﴾): That is, to that religion which Allah has prescribed for you, which He enjoined upon Noah and revealed to you, O Muhammad. So invite the servants of Allah.

*"And be upright as you have been commanded"* (﴿وَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ﴾): That is, remain steadfast in acting upon it, do not deviate from it, and persist in it as Allah has commanded you.

*"And do not follow their desires"* (﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ﴾): That is, do not follow the desires of the polytheists and the People of the Scripture, so that you abandon the *ḥanīfiyyah* (the pure, upright monotheistic faith) with which you were sent, for it is the truth.

*"And say, 'I believe in what Allah has revealed of Scripture'"* (﴿وَقُلْ آمَنتُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن كِتَابٍ﴾): That is, you are not like those who believe in some and disbelieve in others.

*"And I have been commanded to do justice among you"* (﴿وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ﴾): That is, my Lord has commanded me to judge between you with *'adl* (justice), which is the opposite of *jawr* (oppression).

*"Allah is our Lord and your Lord"* (﴿ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾): That is, our Creator and your Creator, our Provider and your Provider, our God and your God.

*"For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds"* (﴿لَنَآ أَعْمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ﴾): Each of us will be recompensed for his deed, whether good or evil.

*"There is no argument between us and you"* (﴿لَا حُجَّةَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ﴾): That is, there is no need for disputation now that the truth has become manifest.

*"Allah will gather us together"* (﴿ٱللَّهُ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا﴾): That is, on the Day of Resurrection.

*"And those who argue about Allah"* (﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآجُّونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾): That is, those who dispute concerning the religion of Allah, [after it has been accepted by] His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

*"After it has been responded to"* (﴿مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ٱسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ﴾): That is, after it was accepted through faith, owing to the manifestness of his miracle. They are the Jews.

*"Their argument is void"* (﴿حُجَّتُهُمْ دَاحِضَةٌ﴾): That is, false in the sight of their Lord.

*"And upon them is wrath"* (﴿وَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ﴾): That is, from Allah, and for them is a severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

**Meaning of the verses:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿فَلِذَلِكَ فَٱدْعُ﴾, that is, to that true religion, which is Islam, which Allah has prescribed for you, which He enjoined upon Noah and revealed to you. So invite all people, Arab and non-Arab, for it is the religion of Allah, which does not accept any religion other than it. A person is not perfected in his morals, knowledge and manners, nor is he made happy in both abodes, except by it. And remain steadfast upon it as your Lord has commanded you; do not deviate from it, nor equate anything else with it, for it is the straight path from which none deviates except the one destined to perish. ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, nor the desires of the polytheists, nor the desires of the People of the Scripture. And say, plainly and clearly, ﴿آمَنتُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن كِتَابٍ﴾, so I do not believe in some and disbelieve in others, as you do, O assembly of Jews and Christians. And say to them: my Lord has commanded me to be just among you in judgment when you come before me for judgment, just as I do not differentiate between you when I consider you equal in disbelief. Everyone who is not upon the Islam upon which Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus were, and upon which I and my companions are today, is a disbeliever and one of the people of the Fire.

And His saying ﴿ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾, that is: He commanded me to say to you, "Allah is our Lord and your Lord," since there is no lord other than Him; He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything. ﴿لَنَآ أَعْمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ﴾, and each of us will be recompensed for his deed: an evil deed by its like, and a good deed by ten times its like. However, the disbeliever has no good deed, as long as he has disbelieved in the foundation of the religion, not believing in Allah, His meeting, His revelation, or His Messenger. And His saying ﴿لَا حُجَّةَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ﴾, that is: today, since the truth has become manifest and the dawn has broken for one who has two eyes. So there is no call for disputation and contention with you, O People of the Two Scriptures, Jews and Christians. ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, since the final return is to Him and not to other than Him. He will judge between us concerning what we differed about: He will decree for the people of truth salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise, and He will decree for the people of falsehood the Fire and abiding in it.

And His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآجُّونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, in the religion of Allah, [i.e., against] the Prophet and the believers, desiring to turn them back to their falsehood, after the Messenger has been responded to and people have entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. ﴿حُجَّتُهُمْ دَاحِضَةٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, that is, void. ﴿وَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ﴾, that is, from their Lord, and for them is a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter. This verse was revealed concerning the Jews in Medina who set themselves up as opponents of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), disputing with them, desiring to create doubt in them about Islam and to bring them back to the idolatry of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance). This was before the Messenger's (ﷺ) migration to Medina. Allah the Exalted responded to them and silenced them with this verse, threatening them with wrath and severe punishment.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The obligation of inviting the nations of the world to Islam, since there is no salvation for humanity except through Islam.

2. The prohibition of following the desires of the people of desires (*ahl al-ahwā'*, i.e., those who follow innovation and personal inclinations), of walking with them, and of agreeing with them in their falsehood.

3. The obligation of steadfastness upon Islam in creed, worship, judicial rulings, manners and ethics.

4. The necessity of abandoning argument and contention with the People of the Scripture, and likewise with the people of desires and innovation, because we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood. How can we dispute with them, when what is obligatory is that they submit, and that suffices.

"Indeed, those who dispute about the Hour": that is, those who argue about the Hour, doubting its occurrence.

"Allah is Gentle with His servants": that is, He is kind to both the righteous and the wicked, as evidenced by the fact that they disobey Him while He provides for them and does not punish them.

"Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter": that is, whoever desires through his deed the reward of the Hereafter.

"We increase for him in his tillage": that is, We multiply his reward, a good deed being rewarded tenfold and more.

"And whoever desires the tillage of this world": that is, whoever desires through his deed the enjoyment of worldly life and its good things.

"We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter": that is, We give him of it what has been decreed for him, and he has no portion or share in the Hereafter.

"Or do they have partners who have legislated for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?": that is, rather, they have partners from among the devils who have legislated for them in religion.

"What Allah has not permitted": that is, what Allah the Exalted has not legislated, which is polytheism (shirk).

"Had it not been for a decisive word, they would have been judged between": that is, had it not been for the decisive word by which Allah decreed the delay of the punishment until the Day of Resurrection, He would have destroyed them today for their polytheism and saved the believers.

**The meaning of the verses:**

Allah the Exalted informs His Messenger and the believers that He is the One who sent down the Book, that is the Qur'an, with truth and sincerity, and sent down the Balance, for the purpose of establishing truth on earth and nullifying falsehood. Therefore none is worshipped but Allah, and none rules except by the law of Allah, and in this lies the perfection of humanity and its happiness. His words, "And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near," mean: what could make you know the nearness of the Hour? It is divine revelation and nothing else. His words, "Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it," mean: those who do not believe in the Last Resurrection and the recompense therein are the ones who press for its coming before its time, and they hasten the Messenger about it, saying, "When is the Hour?" As for the believers in resurrection and recompense, they are fearful, that is, apprehensive of its occurrence, because they do not know their fate therein and do not know whether they will be headed toward happiness or misery. His words, "And they know that it is the truth," mean: the believers know that the Hour is true and certain to occur, when Allah will judge among His servants and recompense each one for his deed, and will exact from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed. Therefore it is certain to occur and will never fail.

His words, "Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in far error," inform, with emphasis, that those who doubt the Hour and argue about the validity of its occurrence are in error far from guidance, rectitude and correctness, and there is no hope for them to return to the right path and guidance on this matter of creed.

His words, "Allah is Gentle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty," inform that He is kind to His servants, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked. Disbelievers deny Him and the disobedient disobey Him, yet He feeds and waters them, pardons them, and does not destroy them for their sins; this is among the evidences of His kindness to them. "He provides for whom He wills," that is, He widens provision for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills, according to what their upbringing requires. Wealth is therefore no proof of approval, nor poverty of displeasure. He is the Strong, the Capable whom nothing can overpower, the Mighty in exacting retribution from whoever He wills to punish.

His words, "Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter, We increase for him his tillage," are among the manifestations of His kindness to His servants: whoever among them desires by his deed the reward of the Hereafter and what Allah has prepared therein for the believing God-fearing, We increase his reward, that is, multiply the reward of his good deed from ten up to seven hundred, and multiply further for whom He wills. This is a denunciation of them and an announcement of severe anger because of their polytheism, which the devils adorned for them, diverting them from the true religion to falsehood. Therefore He says, "Had it not been for a decisive word, they would have been judged between," that is, had it not been that He decreed to delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, He would have punished them in this world and destroyed them before the Hereafter, because they adopted a religion He had not legislated for them. This is a warning to the polytheists who took ignorance, polytheism and idol-worship as their religion and turned away from the religion of Allah, which He enjoined upon Noah, revealed to Muhammad, the seal of His messengers, and enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them.

**Guidance of the verses:**

3. Those who seek to hasten the Hour are the disbelievers who deny it.
4. Explanation of Allah's kindness to His servants; to Him belong praise, grace and thanks.
5. Explanation of the obligation to correct intentions, for the acceptance or rejection of deeds depends on them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 42, verses 22–26:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa huwa wāqi'un bihim﴾ (and it will befall them): That is, the recompense for what they earned of falsehood and polytheism will descend upon them, and they will be punished by it without doubt.

﴿Wa lladhīna āmanū wa 'amilū al-ṣāliḥāt﴾ (And those who believed and did righteous deeds): They believed in Allah, in His meeting, in His signs and in His Messenger, performed the obligatory duties, and avoided the prohibited things.

﴿Fī rawḍāti al-jannāt﴾ (in the gardens of the paradises): That is, they will be in the gardens of Paradise, and a rawḍa (garden meadow) in Paradise is the most pleasant place in it.

﴿Lahum mā yashā'ūna 'inda rabbihim﴾ (For them is whatever they wish with their Lord): That is, for them therein is whatever their souls desire and their eyes find delight in, in the presence of their Lord.

﴿Qul lā as'alukum 'alayhi ajran﴾ (Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it): That is, say, O our Messenger, to your people: I do not ask you for any reward, meaning any recompense, for conveying the message.

﴿Illā al-mawaddata fī al-qurbā﴾ (except affection for the near of kin): That is, but I ask you to love my relatives, so that you do not harm me and prevent me from the people until I convey my Lord's message.

﴿Wa man yaqtarif ḥasanatan﴾ (And whoever earns a good deed): That is, whoever acquires a good deed by speech or righteous action.

﴿Nazid lahu fīhā ḥusnā﴾ (We will increase for him therein good): That is, We will multiply it for him manifold.

﴿Am yaqūlūna iftará 'alā Allāhi kadhibā﴾ (Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?): That is, do these polytheists say that Muhammad has invented a lie against Allah, attributing to Him the Qur'an, when it is neither his speech nor his revelation?

﴿Fa-in yasha' Allāhu yakhtim 'alā qalbik﴾ (If Allah willed, He would seal upon your heart): That is, if Allah, exalted is He, willed, He would seal upon your heart and make you forget the Qur'an, meaning that Allah is able to prevent you from fabricating against Him as the polytheists claim.

﴿Wa yamḥu Allāhu al-bāṭila wa yuḥiqqu al-ḥaqqa﴾ (And Allah effaces falsehood and establishes truth): That is, it is the way of Allah, exalted is He, that He effaces falsehood.

﴿Bi-kalimātih﴾ (by His words): That is, by the Qur'anic verses; and He has effaced falsehood and established truth by the Qur'an.

﴿Wa huwa alladhī yaqbalu al-tawbata 'an 'ibādih﴾ (And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants): That is, He, exalted is He, is the One who accepts the repentance of those among His servants who repent.

﴿Wa ya'fū 'ani al-sayyi'āt﴾ (and pardons misdeeds): That is, He does not hold to account for them those who repent of them. This is the true God, not the idols, which have absolutely no share in what belongs to Allah.

﴿Wa yastajību lladhīna āmanū wa 'amilū al-ṣāliḥāt﴾ (And He responds to those who believed and did righteous deeds): That is, Allah, exalted is He, answers His servants who believed in Him and did righteous deeds in what they asked of Him, and gives them their request.

﴿Wa yazīdahum min faḍlih﴾ (and increases them from His bounty): That is, He gives them what they asked and gives them, beyond that, what they did not ask of good.

﴿Wa al-kāfirūna lahum 'adhābun shadīd﴾ (And the disbelievers will have a severe punishment): That is, and the disbelievers in Allah, His Messenger, the meeting with Allah and His signs, will have a severe punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: "You see the wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection fearful of what they earned," that is, fearful of the recompense for what they earned of polytheism and sins, "and it will befall them, descending upon them without doubt." His saying, ﴿Dhālika huwa al-faḍl al-kabīr﴾ (That is the great bounty): that which Allah has informed them they will have, of the gardens of Paradise and other things, is the great bounty which Allah has bestowed upon them.

His saying, ﴿Qul lā as'alukum 'alayhi ajran illā al-mawaddata fī al-qurbā﴾: Allah commands His Messenger to say to his people among the polytheists: "I do not ask you for any wealth in return for my conveying to you the call of my Lord to faith in Him and His oneness, so that you may be complete and happy. His saying, ﴿Innahu 'alīmun bi-dhāti al-ṣudūr﴾: by the breadth of His knowledge and the greatness of His power, He effaced falsehood and established truth by the Qur'an. Had the Qur'an been fabricated, it would not have effaced falsehood nor established truth. His saying: ﴿Wa huwa alladhī yaqbalu al-tawbata 'an 'ibādih﴾ (And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants): that is, if they turn to Him in repentance, ﴿wa ya'fū 'ani al-sayyi'āt﴾ (and pardons misdeeds), not holding them to account for them, and He knows what they do in secret and openly and recompenses each for what they did, and He is over all things capable.

His saying, ﴿Wa yastajību lladhīna āmanū wa 'amilū al-ṣāliḥāt﴾ (And He responds to those who believed and did righteous deeds): that is, He answers their supplication in what they ask, and increases them from His bounty, giving them what they did not ask. How great is His generosity and how vast His mercy! This is for those who believed and did righteous deeds. As for the disbelievers, they will have a severe punishment.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the right of kinship and the obligation of affection toward it, and honoring and respecting the kinship of the Messenger ﷺ.

2- Clearing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of fabricating against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

3- The multiplication of good deeds, and Allah's appreciation of the righteous deeds of His believing servants.

4- The obligation of repentance and Allah's acceptance of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to repent to Allah one hundred times a day. Repentance has three conditions: immediate cessation of the sin, seeking forgiveness, and regret for having committed the sin by abandoning an obligation or doing a prohibited act. If the sin involves the right of a human being, a fourth condition is added: release from the human being by rendering the right or seeking his pardon.

5- Allah's promise to answer the supplication of believing servants who do righteous deeds, who are the friends of Allah: if they ask, He gives them; if they seek His refuge, He protects them; and if they seek His help, He helps them. O Allah, make us among them and gather us in their company.

﴿Wa mā baththa fīhimā min dābbah﴾: that is, He scattered and spread, from everything that crawls upon the earth, among people and others.

﴿Wa huwa ‘alā jam‘ihim idhā yashā'u qadīr﴾: that is, He is capable of gathering them for the Resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense.

﴿Wa lākin yunazzilu bi-qadarin mā yashā'﴾: that is, He sends down provisions in whatever measure He wills, so He expands and restricts.

﴿Innahu bi-‘ibādihi khabīrun baṣīr﴾: that is, He is aware of the conditions of His servants, since some of them are corrupted by wealth, some are improved by it, some are improved by poverty, and some are corrupted by it.

﴿Wa huwa alladhī yunazzilu al-ghayth min ba‘di mā qanaṭū﴾: that is, the rain, after they had despaired of its descent.

﴿Wa yanshuru raḥmatahu﴾: that is, the blessings and benefits of the rain across every plain, mountain, plant and animal.

﴿Wa huwa al-Walī al-Ḥamīd﴾: that is, the One who takes charge of His believing servants, who is good to them, and who is praised by them.

﴿Wa mā baththa fīhimā min dābbah﴾: that is, He scattered and spread, from everything that crawls upon the earth, among people and others.

﴿Wa huwa ‘alā jam‘ihim idhā yashā'u qadīr﴾: that is, He is capable of gathering them for the Resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense.

﴿Wa mā aṣābakum min muṣībah﴾: that is, a trial or hardship of the hardships, such as sickness and poverty.

﴿Bimā kasabat aydīkum﴾: that is, because of sins and wrongdoings.

This begins a presentation of the manifestations of power, knowledge and wisdom that necessitate God's lordship, which in turn entails His divinity and the worship due to Him. The Most High said: ﴿Wa law basaṭa Allāh﴾, that is, the Lord of the servants, expanded provision for them, they would have transgressed upon the earth, some of them would have oppressed others and wronged one another, and this would have entailed great corruption on earth, by which life in its entirety might be brought to a halt.

﴿Wa lākin yunazzilu bi-qadarin mā yashā'﴾: that is, He sends down provisions in measured quantities according to His management of the lives of His servants. This is shown by His saying: ﴿Innahu bi-‘ibādihi khabīrun baṣīr﴾, that is, He is aware of what the lives of His servants require, with their limited lifespans, their measured and weighed deeds, and their outcomes known from eternity. The sending down of rain in specific quantities and measures, in specific places and under specific conditions, is an act established only upon overpowering power and perfect knowledge. He withholds rain from His servants so that they become barren and dry, until they despair and their helplessness and the helplessness of the gods they worship, falsely, become manifest and obvious, since these gods do not deserve worship in any way. Then He sends down the rain and spreads mercy, so that provisions, goods and blessings become general. He is the Walī, to whom no one else's guardianship is suitable, the Ḥamīd, that is, praised for the works of His kindness, the bounties of His goodness and the manifestations of His mercy. He is the Walī in truth and the praised in truth. Another manifestation is in His saying, Exalted is He, among His signs that indicate His existence, power, knowledge and wisdom, which necessitate His lordship over all His creation and entail His divinity over all His servants: ﴿Khalqu al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ﴾, the creation of the heavens and the earth with their wondrous attributes, and what He scattered and spread in them of living creatures that crawl upon the earth, or angels that glorify in the heavens.

Why, then, is other than Him worshipped among His creatures, and His worship abandoned? Beyond this manifestation of creation, provision and management there is another: His power to gather all His creation in one place, and when? Every affliction that strikes a person in this life results from disobedience to God in regard to the laws, legislations and patterns He has established. The greatest indication of this is that a past law is suspended and its effect halted, so that the servant earns a sin but is not held accountable for it, by God's pardon toward him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Wa ya‘fū ‘an kathīr﴾. So to Him belongs praise and to Him belongs grace.

The sky is above them and the earth beneath them; if He wills, He causes the earth to swallow them or drops the sky upon them in pieces. Where, then, is the escape? The answer is to God alone, by submission to Him and obedience in compliance, and in that lies their salvation, their dignity and their honor, in addition to their happiness and perfection in both lives. His saying: ﴿Wa mā lakum min dūnillāhi min waliyyin wa lā naṣīr﴾, that is, you have, O people, with your weakness, no guardian other than God who will take charge of you, and no helper who will help you. So flee to God by faith in Him and submission to Him, and you will be saved and made happy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 42, verse 32–35:

Explanation of the words:

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾: That is, He halts the blowing of the wind, so there is neither breeze nor violent storm.

﴿So they remain motionless on its surface﴾: That is, the ships stand still and remain stationary, held fast upon the back of the sea.

﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾: That is, in these manifestations, namely the creation of ships and seas, the subjecting of the seas, the sailing of ships, and their standing still when the winds are calm, there are clear proofs of the existence of God and of His power, knowledge and wisdom.

﴿For every steadfast, grateful one﴾: That is, these signs are not seen or benefited from except by one who is patient in the face of hardships and trials, and grateful for blessings and favours.

﴿Or He destroys them for what they have earned﴾: That is, and if He wills, He makes the winds into violent storms, destroying those ships and drowning them with their occupants because of the sins of their people, and He is over all things competent.

﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know﴾: That is, those who deny the signs of God among the polytheists will know when the storms rage, the ships are tossed, and they fear drowning.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues in mentioning the manifestations of lordship, which entail the divinity of God and the obligation of worshipping Him alone, apart from any other. So He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And among His signs are the ships running in the sea like mountains﴾. That is, and among His proofs against you, O servants of God, which indicate His power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy as well, are these ships running in the sea like lofty mountains moving from region to region by God's subjecting of the seas and sending of the winds, and they run for your benefit, carrying passengers and goods from one region to another. This is a manifestation of God's power and mercy. If He, exalted is He, wills to still the wind, it stills and does not blow nor breathe any breeze at all, so the ships stand and become motionless on the surface of the water and do not move. And if He also wills, He sends upon them violent winds, and they are tossed and drown with what is in them and those in them, and that is because of the sins of their people; for the established and settled rule is that there is no calamity except by sin. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, so they remain motionless on its surface﴾.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾. That is, indeed in these manifestations, namely the creation of ships and seas, the subjecting of the seas, the sailing of ships upon them, and their standing still when the wind is calm, are strong and clear proofs of the existence of God and of His power, knowledge, mercy and wisdom. But they are not seen or benefited from by the likes of cattle; rather they are the portion of every servant who is patient in obeying God and in His trials, and grateful for His bounties and blessings upon him.

And His saying: ﴿Or He destroys them for what they have earned﴾, and His saying: ﴿And He pardons much﴾. That is, He does not take to account for every sin, for He may pardon many sins. For if He punished every sin and held every transgression to account, no one would remain on the earth, since there is no one who does not sin, except those protected from sin among the prophets and messengers, for they do not sin. Yet their forebears and descendants may sin, and so they perish. And from where would they be found!?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know that for them there is no escape﴾. That is, when the wind is violent and the ships are tossed and near to drowning, then the polytheists who dispute with the Messenger of God and argue against the divine revelation and deny it will know that in this state there is for them no refuge, no escape from God except to Him. So they cry out in supplication to God alone, as He said: ﴿And when they board the ship, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The manifestations of God's lordship and divinity over His creation.

2- The virtue of patience and gratitude, and the excellence of those who are patient and grateful.

3- The establishment of the rule that there is no calamity except by sin, together with God's pardon of much.

4- At the sight of punishment, a person knows his Lord and knows no other.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 42, verse 36–41:

Explanation of the words:

"Whatever you have been given of anything" (fa-ma utītum min shay'): that is, whatever you have been given of the enjoyments of this world, such as wealth, children, food, drink, clothing, dwelling, marriage, and mounts.

"Then it is the enjoyment of the life of this world" (fa-matā'u al-ḥayāt al-dunyā): that is, one enjoys it for a time, then it passes away and does not remain.

"And what is with Allah is better and more lasting" (wa-mā 'inda Allāh khayrun wa-abqā): that is, what is with Allah of the reward of the Hereafter is better in its kind and more lasting in its duration.

"For those who believe and upon their Lord they rely" (lilladhīna āmanū wa-'alā rabbihim yatawakkalūn): that is, what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who possess the following qualities:

Faith; reliance upon Allah; avoiding the major sins and indecencies; forgiveness toward those who wrong them; responding to their Lord in everything He calls them to, whether by doing or by abstaining; establishing the prayer; consulting among themselves; spending from what Allah has provided them; and defending themselves when they are oppressed. These are ten qualities, and whoever possesses them will have what Allah has prepared for him on the day he meets Him, which is better than the entire enjoyment of this world.

"And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it" (wa-jazā'u sayyi'atin sayyi'atun mithluhā): that is, the recompense for the wrongdoer's evil is his punishment with what Allah has made obligatory for him.

"But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon Allah" (fa-man 'afā wa-aṣlaḥa fa-ajruhu 'alā Allāh): that is, whoever pardons the one who wronged him and makes reconciliation between himself and him, his reward is secured with Allah.

This is the man before he believes, submits and becomes good. When he believes, submits and does good, his nature changes, his origin is purified, and he becomes one who gives thanks in times of blessing and is patient in times of affliction.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. By the judgment of His authority over the earth and the heavens, He disposes of them as He wills. Among the guidance of these verses:

2. Those who call to God must convey what God requires of His servants, and nothing will harm them after that.

3. A description of human nature and condition before it is refined by faith, certainty and acts of obedience.

4. God has absolute disposal over the whole of the kingdom, so it is not valid to object to Him in anything. He gives and withholds for lofty wisdoms that the minds of the servants cannot grasp.

5. There exists infertility in men and infertility in women, and there is no harm in permissible and lawful treatment when one feels infertility or barrenness. As for what has now appeared of sperm banks, and conception by pouring the semen of a stallion [male] into the womb of a barren woman, and the like, these are the deeds of atheists who do not owe God obedience or submission to His decree, and even if they fast, pray and claim to be believers, they have no shame, and there is no faith for one who has no shame. After that tremendous depiction of the terrors and conditions of the wrongdoers on the plains of Resurrection, the Lord, exalted is He, asked His servants to respond to Him in what He asked of them, in order to save themselves from the Fire. He said: ﴿Respond to your Lord﴾, meaning: respond to Him in what He has called you to, namely *tawhid* and acts of obedience, before the opportunity is lost, and that is before death and before the Day of Resurrection, the Day which, when it comes, cannot be turned back by God. For none can repel it except God, and God has informed us that He will not repel it, so who then could repel it? So hasten to repent to your Lord before it comes, for on that Day you will have no refuge to flee to from the punishment, and you will have no denial by which you could deny your sins, since they have been gathered for you in one Book which leaves no small or great sin without counting it precisely. This is what the first verse [47] indicates, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from God which cannot be turned back. You will have no refuge that Day, nor will you have any denial.﴾

His saying, in the second verse [48]: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they did not respond to their Lord in what He called them to, namely *tawhid* and obedience, ﴿then We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾, to count their deeds and keep account of them for them and recompense them for them. ﴿Your duty is only to deliver﴾, that is, your duty is only to deliver the message. You have delivered it and your obligation is discharged, so do not be concerned about them and do not grieve over their turning away.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us﴾, that is, a blessing such as abundance of provision, health of body, and great wealth and children, ﴿he rejoices in it﴾ with the rejoicing of insolence and exultation. This "man" is the disbeliever, or the ignorant one who is weak in faith.

﴿And if an evil befalls them﴾, that is, straitened living, illness and poverty, ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾, that is, because of the sins they committed, ﴿indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, quickly forgetting the blessing and the Bestower of it, and falling into despair and hopelessness. This is the man before he believes, submits and becomes good. When he believes, submits and does good, his nature changes, his origin is purified, and he becomes one who gives thanks in times of blessing and is patient in times of affliction.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. By the judgment of His authority over the earth and the heavens, He disposes of them as He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills among people barren, neither bearing nor begetting children. This proceeds from a knowledge that encompasses all things and a power to which all things are subjected, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ It is therefore obligatory for the servant to submit to his Lord regarding what He has granted and given him, for God gives for a wisdom and withholds for a wisdom, and it is folly to object to the decree of God.

**The guidance of the verses:**

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. The obligation to respond to God in everything to which He calls the servant, and that is before one seeks a response and is not granted it.

2. Those who call to God must convey what God requires of His servants, and nothing will harm them after that.

3. A description of human nature and condition before it is refined by faith, certainty and acts of obedience.

4. God has absolute disposal over the whole of the kingdom, so it is not valid to object to Him in anything. He gives and withholds for lofty wisdoms that the minds of the servants cannot grasp.

5. There exists infertility in men and infertility in women, and there is no harm in permissible and lawful treatment when one feels infertility or barrenness. As for what has now appeared of sperm banks, and conception by pouring the semen of a stallion [male] into the womb of a barren woman, and the like, these are the deeds of atheists who do not owe God obedience or submission to His decree, and even if they fast, pray and claim to be believers, they have no shame, and there is no faith for one who has no shame. Their conduct is sufficiently ugly in that it exposes the private parts without saving a life or seeking the pleasure of God, the Lord of the earth and the heavens.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 42, verses 51–53:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Except by revelation, or from behind a veil⦘: that is, a hidden, swift notification, either while awake or in a dream; or He speaks to him from behind a veil, so he hears the speech without seeing the Essence.

﴿Or sends a messenger⦘: that is, or He sends an angel in the form of a human, who speaks to him, conveying from Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Indeed, He is Most High, All-Wise⦘: that is, Allah, the Exalted, is high above all His creation, and All-Wise in the management of His creation.

﴿And thus We have revealed to you⦘: that is, just as We used to reveal to all Our messengers, We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, this Qur'an.

﴿A spirit of Our command⦘: that is, revelation and mercy from Our command, which We reveal to you.

﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was⦘: that is, before this you did not know what the Book is, nor what faith (al-iman) is, which consists of statement, action and belief.

﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants⦘: that is, We made the Qur'an a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants to Our path.

﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path⦘: that is, Islam.

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah are all matters returned⦘: that is, the affairs of all servants will return to Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High, All-Wise﴾ — He informs that it is not the condition of any human, whoever he may be, that Allah speaks to him except by revelation, by informing him through a swift, hidden means: inspiration (ilham) or a dream, so that he understands from Allah what is cast into his heart, certain that it is the speech of Allah cast to him. This is one method. The second is that Allah speaks to him and he hears His speech without seeing His Essence, as He spoke to Musa (peace be upon him) on more than one occasion. The third is that He sends to him a messenger, such as Jibril (peace be upon him), who conveys the speech of his Lord, the Exalted. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿Most High, All-Wise﴾: high above His creation, and wise in His management of His creation.

His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ — that is, just as We used to reveal to all Our messengers, We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, a spirit, which is the Qur'an. It is called a spirit because hearts are given life by it, just as bodies are given life by spirits. His saying ﴿from Our command﴾ means: which We reveal to you, encompassing the commands, prohibitions, promises and warnings. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ — that is, the Qur'an, nor faith, which is belief, statement and action.

His saying: ﴿But We made it a light﴾ — that is, We made the Qur'an a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants to faith in Us, to our Oneness, and to seeking Our pleasure by doing what We love and avoiding what We dislike.

His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ — that is, and indeed you, O Our messenger, guide to a straight path, which is the Islamic religion. His saying ﴿the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — that is, by creation, dominion and servitude. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah are all matters returned﴾ — that is, to Him, the Exalted, is the destination of everything and the return of everything, for He is the true Owner and the Manager of the affairs of all creatures. Therefore, it is obligatory to entrust the matter to Him and to be content with His judgment and decree, having trust in Him and in His sufficiency.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the methods of revelation, which are three: the first is casting into the heart while awake or in a dream; the second is that Allah speaks to the Prophet without his seeing His Essence, the Mighty and Majestic, as He spoke to Musa at Mount Tur and spoke to Muhammad ﷺ in the highest realm; and the third is that the angel is sent to him, either in his angelic form or in the form of a man from the children of Adam, and he reveals to him what Allah wills of His command.

2- The noble Qur'an is a spirit by which dead hearts are given life, just as bodies are given life by spirits.

3- The Qur'an is a light by which one is guided in life, so that the paths of happiness and the ways of salvation are known through it.
